name: glob
description: List files in the workspace whose name or path matches a shell pattern. Use to find out what exists before reading or searching it.

pattern.description: A shell pattern: * ? and [...]. Without a slash it matches the file name anywhere in the tree, so "*.py" finds every Python file. With a slash it matches the whole path, and * spans directories, so "src/*_test.py" finds them at any depth under src.

path.description: Directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Must resolve inside it. Defaults to the whole workspace.

type.description: What to list. Directories are usually not what you want; the default is files only.

max_results.description: Stop after this many paths and say so. Raise it only when the truncated list was genuinely not enough.

output_schema.description: One path per line, relative to the workspace root and sorted, so two runs over an unchanged tree agree byte for byte. A final "[glob] output truncated: ..." line is appended when max_results was reached. Matching nothing is a successful search: the output is a single "[glob] no matches for ..." line and the exit code is 0.

exit_codes.0: success (the search ran; it matched something or it did not)
exit_codes.2: invalid input (stdin was not a JSON object, or a parameter is missing or the wrong type)
exit_codes.3: not found (the search path does not exist)
exit_codes.4: not permitted (the search path resolves outside the workspace root, or is not readable)
